lead: A solid electrolyte is a solid phase (crystalline ceramic or ion-exchange polymer) that conducts one kind of ion and almost no electrons, so a cell built on it gives a Nernst EMF for that species; the same material in amperometric mode gives a current that is linear in concentration. A surface acoustic wave sensor launches a ripple along a piezoelectric surface and reads how a film on the path slows it down. You meet the first in car lambda sensors and the second in wireless torque and temperature tags.
prereq: You need: the Nernst cell from 5.2 and piezoelectric transducers and ultrasonic waves from Unit 4.

sections.h3: Solid electrolytes: one ion, one EMF

blocks.text: A solid electrolyte is a solid phase (crystalline ceramic or ion-exchange polymer) that conducts one kind of ion and almost no electrons. The mobile ion carries the current, so the material is selective by construction. Common pairs: yttria-stabilised zirconia (YSZ) conducts O²⁻, sodium beta-alumina conducts Na⁺, Nafion conducts H⁺, and lanthanum fluoride conducts F⁻.

blocks.where: σ is the ionic conductivity in S/m; σ₀ is a prefactor in S/m; E_a is the activation energy in J; k = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J/K is Boltzmann's constant; T is the temperature in kelvin.

blocks.text: E_a is large, so useful conductivity arrives only at a few hundred degrees Celsius. YSZ needs roughly 700 °C. A cold zirconia sensor gives almost no signal, which is why every lambda sensor carries a heater.

In potentiometric mode two electrodes on the electrolyte see two oxygen partial pressures, p₁ and p₂. The cell gives a Nernst EMF: E = (RT / 4F) · ln(p₁ / p₂). Here R = 8.314 J/(mol·K), T is in kelvin, F = 96485 C/mol, and the 4 is the number of electrons per O₂ molecule. This is the zirconia oxygen cell of 5.2. The output is logarithmic, and a reference gas is mandatory.

Amperometric mode puts a diffusion barrier over the cathode and holds the cell at a voltage that pumps away every oxygen molecule that arrives. The current then saturates at I_lim = (4F·A·D / δ) · C. A is the barrier area in m², D the diffusion coefficient in m²/s, δ the barrier thickness in m, and C the oxygen concentration in mol/m³. The reading is linear in C and needs no reference gas.

A surface acoustic wave (SAW) travels along the surface of a piezoelectric crystal, with its energy confined to about one wavelength of depth. Quartz, lithium niobate (LiNbO₃) and zinc oxide (ZnO) on silicon are the usual substrates.

An interdigital transducer (IDT) is two interleaved comb-shaped metal electrodes; the centre-to-centre spacing of neighbouring fingers is half an acoustic wavelength, so the finger pattern repeats every wavelength. An RF voltage across the combs makes the surface ripple. The wave runs to a second IDT, which converts it back into a voltage. That pair is a delay line; adding reflectors or closing the loop makes a resonator.

blocks.where: f is the operating frequency in Hz; Δf is its shift; v is the surface wave velocity in m/s; Δv is its change, signed; λ is the acoustic wavelength in m, set by the IDT finger spacing. The IDT fixes λ, and f = v/λ, so the frequency falls when the wave slows. The shift scales with mass per unit area, not total mass.

blocks.text: Mass loading or a soft, viscoelastic film on the delay path slows the wave and adds attenuation. A 0.10 % velocity drop becomes a 0.10 % frequency drop. Wireless passive tags use an antenna, an IDT and a reflector with no battery; a torque twisting the substrate changes the delay, and so does temperature.
Only a few universities teach the coupling-of-modes design of these transducers. It predicts the IDT response from the finger geometry and the reflections inside the comb.

items: Catalytic gas detector (pellistor): a heated platinum coil burns the gas, and the temperature rise changes the coil resistance.
Surface plasmon resonance: light reflected from a thin metal film shows a sharp dip at one angle because the energy couples into a surface plasmon; binding on the film shifts that angle.
Optical chemical sensor: a reagent changes colour or fluorescence when the analyte binds, and the change is read as absorbance or intensity.

blocks.text: Pick the solid electrolyte when you need selectivity to one ion at high temperature, and the SAW device when you need a passive, wireless, small mass or force sensor.

figure.caption: The 100 MHz source drives the input transducer; the wave crosses the film-coated delay path and the output transducer feeds a mixer, which is also fed by a 100 MHz reference, giving the 100 kHz difference of the worked example.

spec.title: SAW delay line
spec.aria: A 100 MHz radio source drives an input interdigital transducer, a delay path with an adsorbed film, an output transducer and a mixer; a 100 MHz reference also feeds the mixer, which reads the frequency shift.

examples.question: A SAW delay line runs at 100 MHz on quartz. An adsorbed film slows the surface wave by 0.10 %. Find the frequency shift, and check it against a mass sensitivity of 50 kHz per nanogram for a 2.0 ng film.
steps: Fractional velocity change: Δv/v = −0.10 % = −0.0010. The minus sign means the wave is slower.
For a delay line, f = v/λ and λ is fixed by the IDT, so Δf/f = Δv/v = −0.0010. The fractional frequency shift has the same size and sign as the velocity shift.
Δf = −0.0010 × 100 MHz = −0.100 MHz = −100 kHz. The frequency falls by 100 kHz.

The two numbers agree, so the 0.10 % slowing is consistent with a 2.0 ng film under the linear mass-loading assumption. To test the assumption itself you need the film thickness compared with the acoustic wavelength.
examples.answer: Δf = −100 kHz, a 100 kHz downward shift, matching the mass estimate of 100 kHz.
examples.check:
f = 100e6
dv = -0.0010
df = dv * f
print(df / 1e3)
print(50e3 * 2.0 / 1e3)

traps: Applying the Sauerbrey equation, a bulk quartz-crystal-microbalance result, to a SAW delay line, and forgetting that the shift follows mass per unit area, not total mass.
Reversing the Nernst ratio: the EMF rises when the sample oxygen falls, so p_reference sits on top of the fraction.
Believing a solid electrolyte conducts electrons like a wire. It conducts one ion, and a potentiometric cell still needs a reference gas or electrode.
Mixing the two modes: potentiometric is logarithmic and needs a reference; amperometric with a diffusion barrier is linear and needs none.
Ignoring the temperature dependence of σ. A zirconia cell below about 400 °C reads close to zero whatever the oxygen level.

quiz.q: Which ion does yttria-stabilised zirconia conduct, and which ion does Nafion conduct?
quiz.a: YSZ conducts O²⁻ ions; Nafion conducts H⁺ ions.

Two interleaved comb-shaped metal electrodes on a piezoelectric surface; the centre-to-centre spacing of neighbouring fingers is half an acoustic wavelength, so the finger pattern repeats every wavelength. They convert an RF voltage to a surface wave and back.

quiz.q: Why does a zirconia oxygen sensor need a heater?
quiz.a: Ionic conductivity follows σ₀·exp(−E_a/kT) with a large E_a, so at room temperature it is far too low. A few hundred degrees Celsius are needed before the cell delivers a usable EMF.

quiz.q: A zirconia cell at 1000 K sees 0.21 bar on the reference side and 0.01 bar on the sample side. Find the EMF.
A 200 MHz SAW delay line shows a 0.05 % velocity drop. Find the frequency shift.
quiz.a: Δv/v = −0.0005. Since Δf/f = Δv/v, Δf/f = −0.0005, so Δf = −0.0005 × 200 MHz = −100 kHz. The frequency falls by 100 kHz.

quiz.q: Why is an amperometric sensor with a diffusion barrier preferred over a potentiometric cell for the exhaust lambda measurement?
quiz.a: The limiting current is linear in oxygen concentration, needs no reference gas, and is set by diffusion through the barrier, so it is stable against electrode drift. A potentiometric cell is logarithmic and needs a known reference gas.

quiz.q: On a SAW delay line, the frequency shift stops growing as a polymer film gets thicker while the attenuation keeps rising. Explain.
quiz.a: The wave samples only about one wavelength of the film, so extra thickness adds little mass that the wave feels. The film's softness still absorbs energy, so attenuation keeps rising.

beyond: Not for the exam. Solid ion conductors now sit at the centre of solid-state batteries and two-chamber NOx sensors, where the first chamber pumps out oxygen and the second measures the remainder. SAW tags are used in tyre pressure monitoring and in torque measurement on rotating drive shafts, where a battery cannot reach. Search for NASICON CO₂ sensors, yttria-stabilised zirconia lambda sensors, and SAW wireless passive tags to go further.
